name: Trystan

attributes.attribute: the Welsh form of the hero Tristan
wife of King March ap Meirchion
kept Esyllt by reason of the evergreen yew

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Trystan is the Welsh form of the romance hero Tristan. He is also called Drystan and Drystan fab Tallwch. In the Welsh tale he is the hero and Esyllt is the heroine. Esyllt is the wife of King March ap Meirchion. The two eloped to a forest. A rout of soldiers of March laid siege to them. When it seemed Trystan would win, King Arthur came to make a truce. He told the two men to share the woman, one for summer and one for winter. March chose the winter, when the nights are long. Trystan claimed the yew stays green all year. So he said Esyllt would stay with him through winter too. And so he kept her. The figure of Trystan may grow from the lore of the Picts.
